results.readme_quote: checks each one in a real browser with Kane CLI
results.reason: Describes how the tool works internally. A browser cannot observe which engine produced the report.
Shell command. It is not observable in a browser.

results.readme_quote: `rld gate` exits 0 when every claim is true, 1 when a claim is false or stale, 3 when the result is inconclusive, and 4 when the tool itself or Kane failed.
results.reason: Process exit codes are not visible in a browser.

results.readme_quote: It runs previously failed claims first, stops at the first failure, and skips claims that already passed on the same README and build.
results.reason: CLI runtime behaviour. Nothing in the browser shows it.

results.readme_quote: Python 3.11 or newer and Node.js (tested with v24.22.1).
results.reason: Local install requirement, not a browser check.
Install command, not a browser check.

results.readme_quote: To claim it, sign in at testmuai.com, open https://www.testmuai.com/kane-cli/#creditOffer, enter your email and click "Claim Credits".
results.reason: Needs a real account and email, and would spend or claim real credits. Third-party site, outside this README's app.

results.readme_quote: the tool refuses to start when your balance is under 2,000 credits (`RLD_MIN_CREDITS`), runs at most 12 Kane runs per invocation
results.reason: CLI safeguards driven by environment variables. Not observable in a browser.

results.readme_quote: After three blocked rounds the turn is released with a warning. Set `RLD_HOOK=off` to turn the hook off.
results.reason: Claude Code Stop hook behaviour, outside the browser.

results.readme_quote: Every run writes one static page, `report/index.html`, plus screenshots in `report/assets/`.
results.reason: Local file output. The browser only sees the hosted copy, not the files a run writes.

results.readme_quote: `demo-app/` is Hati, a small bill splitter whose README makes eight testable claims.
